_about:
Calibration fixture for the local cloud-egress anonymizer (scripts/dev/calibrate_cloud_anonymizer.py and the span-tagger SCAN step it exercises, paramem.cloud.span_tagger). Fictional payloads only -- no real personal data. Reconstructed 2026-08-25 from the live-gate calibration record; every name, number, address, email and handle is invented. 

Schema: one JSON document with a top-level "payloads" list. Each entry has: "id" (a short descriptive slug, unique within the file); "kind" (one of "transcript", "facts", "dense", "planted", "document" -- what shape of input the payload feeds into the anonymizer); "language" (an ISO 639-1 code); "description" (what the payload exercises, in plain language); "transcript" (a marker-bearing string using "[user]"/"[assistant]" line prefixes, present for every kind except "facts") or "facts" (a list of {subject, predicate, object, relation_type, confidence, speaker_id} objects, present only for kind "facts"); "speaker_id" and "speaker_name" (the session's own speaker; "speaker_name" is null throughout this fixture, matching production's default shape where the speaker is identified by voice enrollment and never states their own name in the text); "expected" (the personal values the anonymizer must recognise, one array per category -- "person", "phone", "email", "address", "profile" -- using the exact surface form expected to be tagged); and "must_not_tag" (near-miss values -- organisation names, platform names, generic domains, digit strings that resemble an in-scope value -- that must stay untagged).

payloads.description: Two phone numbers (a personal mobile and a shared support line) plus one person name, both surfaced under casual urgency language.
payloads.transcript:
[user] Hi, I'm Lena Fischer. Call +49 160 5550177 -- it's urgent!
[assistant] Thanks. If that line is busy, the support desk is 0800 555 0123.
[user] Perfect, I'll try both this afternoon.
[assistant] Noted.

payloads.description: Two person names and two email addresses, one introduced as a cc recipient rather than the message's primary addressee.
payloads.transcript:
[user] Nadia Okonjo asked me to send the quote to omar.haddad@example.com.
[assistant] Understood. Anything else before I file it?
[user] Yes -- copy contracts@example.org and let Felix Braun know.
[assistant] Will do.

payloads.description: One postal address and one recipient name split across two conversational turns (the address is given before the name).
payloads.transcript:
[user] Ship the parcel to Rosenweg 8, 80331 München, please.
[assistant] Got it. Who should I put down as the recipient?
[user] Priya Raman.
[assistant] Recorded.

payloads.description: A relocated office: a postal address and a phone number correction, plus one person name given as a contact to ask for.
payloads.transcript:
[user] Our western office moved to 27 Quay Street, Galway last month.
[assistant] Thanks -- is the number still the same?
[user] No, it's +353 91 555 0146 now. Ask for Jonas Lindgren.

payloads.description: A social handle and a profile URL for the same person, alongside platform-name and generic-domain decoys that must stay untagged.
payloads.transcript:
[user] Mara Lindqvist posts as @mara_lindqvist and her page is linkedin.com/in/mara-lindqvist.
[assistant] Should I check LinkedIn or wiki.example.net for the bio?
[user] Neither -- the repo at github.com/acme-tools has the current one.
[assistant] Understood.

payloads.description: One social handle and one postal address for the same person, introduced through a casual forum reference.
payloads.transcript:
[user] Omar Haddad goes by @omar_h on the forum.
[assistant] Noted. Where does he collect post?
[user] 14 Harbour Lane, Bristol BS1 5TY.

payloads.description: Two people mentioned multiple times across turns, plus an organisation name decoy that has historically been mis-tagged as a person.
payloads.transcript:

[assistant] Did Dana Whitfield join the call?
[user] She did. Alex Turner will send the notes; Harrison & Cole are handling the filing.
[assistant] I'll flag it for Harrison & Cole then.

payloads.description: Two people joining a meeting, with a work email address belonging to only one of them.

[assistant] Do you have a contact address for either of them?

payloads.description: The same first name spoken twice with different capitalisation (sentence-initial vs. mid-sentence), plus a second person's name. Exercises that both casings of the same name are recognised as the same person and share one placeholder rather than minting two.
payloads.transcript:
[user] Lena said she would come by at six.
[assistant] Which Lena -- the one from the choir?
[user] Yes, lena from the choir. Her sister Marta will drive her.
[assistant] Understood.

payloads.description: A German surname appearing in four grammatical forms in one conversation: the full name once, the genitive form twice, and the bare dative surname once, plus an email address built from the same surname. Exercises a known residual: the anonymizer matches exact surfaces only, so the inflected surname forms are not caught by the same match as the full name and can reach the outbound text verbatim even though the full name and the email are correctly scrubbed.
payloads.transcript:
[user] Lena Fischer hat angerufen. Fischers Nummer ist +49 160 5550177.
[assistant] Soll ich Fischers Termin auf morgen verschieben?
[user] Ja, und schick Fischer die Bestätigung an lena.fischer@example.de.
[assistant] Erledigt.

payloads.description: A short exchange with zero in-scope personal values: a build identifier, an internal hostname, a building name and a generic channel name, all of which look superficially identifier-like but must not be tagged under any configured category.
payloads.transcript:
[user] The build 4471-0921 finished on the runner at ci.example.internal.
[assistant] Which building did that run in?
[user] The Fitzgerald Annex, third floor. It was pushed to the Slack channel.
[assistant] Noted.

payloads.description: Twenty-two extracted graph facts: fourteen carry a person or contact endpoint (names, phone numbers, email addresses, postal addresses, a social handle and a profile URL) and eight are plain facts with no personal endpoint at all. Exercises the graph-tier anonymization path (as opposed to the transcript path): the fact structure's own field names must never be tagged, and organisation names must stay untagged even when they resemble the person-name decoy seen in prose.
